citation.title: Data-driven topology optimization of spinodoid metamaterials with seamlessly tunable anisotropy
citation.authors: Li Zheng, Siddhant Kumar, Dennis M. Kochmann
citation.venue: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering
citation.version_coded: Version of record (Delft University of Technology repository copy)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: A neural surrogate replaces repeated finite-element homogenization in the multiscale optimizer, predicting effective stiffness in 0.001 s per sample versus about 5 min for finite-element homogenization.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Appendix B, Table B.1 reports 5 min (300 s) for FEM stiffness calculation and 0.001 s per DNN prediction; 300 / 0.001 = 300,000.
claim.alternatives: Abstract and §6 state that the DNN surrogate speeds multiscale calculations and supplies exact sensitivities; §5 reports four compliance optimization benchmarks.

baseline.classical_method: Finite-element numerical homogenization of spinodoid microstructures within a two-scale compliance optimization; macro comparison also includes classical SIMP (§§3, 5).
baseline.implementation: In-house C++ FEM code for stiffness homogenization; DNN implemented with PyTorch in Python (Appendix B, Table B.1).
baseline.hardware_classical: 16 MPI cores on ETH Zürich Euler IV cluster: two 18-core 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon Gold 6150 processors, 192 GB DDR4 memory (Appendix B, Table B.1).
baseline.hardware_ml: CPU, no parallelization, on four 12-core 2.2 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2650 processors, 256 GB DDR3 memory (Appendix B, Table B.1).
baseline.problem_size: RVE size l × l × l; macro examples include 22,060 and 25,350 linear tetrahedral elements (Appendix B; §5).
baseline.classical_time: 5 min per FEM stiffness computation (Appendix B, Table B.1).
baseline.ml_time: 0.001 s per DNN prediction on one data sample (Appendix B, Table B.1).
baseline.data_generation_cost: FEM stiffness computation takes 5 min per sample; total dataset size or aggregate generation cost not stated (Appendix B, Table B.1; §4.1).
baseline.quality_metric: Effective elastic stiffness tensor for each spinodoid; macro objective is linear-elastic compliance, with relative density constraint (Abstract; §§3–5).
baseline.quality_gap: not stated as a numerical comparison of surrogate prediction error in this paper; the surrogate is described as accurate (§4.1).

R1.evidence: Appendix B, Table B.1: timings compare a DNN stiffness prediction with FEM stiffness homogenization for one sample; no contrary design-quality mismatch is established.

R2.evidence: Appendix B, Table B.1 identifies in-house C++ FEM on 16 MPI cores; solver efficiency or an inefficient baseline is not established by the text.

R3.evidence: Appendix B, Table B.1 reports 10 min DNN training and 5 min per FEM stiffness sample, but no break-even use count or explicit per-query-only qualification.

R4.evidence: Sections 4–5 use DNN-predicted effective stiffness in the multiscale design workflow; returned microstructures are not reported as FE-verified for all outputs.

reporting.n_test_cases: Four macro compliance optimization benchmarks (Appendix B, Table B.1; §5).

notes: The benchmark runtimes are described as rough single-CPU duration estimates; the stiffness FEM and DNN timing use different stated hardware (Appendix B).
